title: QLP eclipse fits of HD 303514 permit unequal stellar radii under a free light and speed model
abstract: We test the equal-radius assumption used in HD 303514 eclipse forecasts. We fit 16 eclipse windows in QLP TESS light curves from eight sectors, with fixed radius ratios from 0.3 to 1.0. Surface brightness, sector light fractions, projected speed and local eclipse geometry are free. Raw and detrended aperture flux both admit substantially unequal radii with almost the same weighted squared loss. The fitted distance from contact changes with the radius choice and flux reduction. This gives a direct limit on shape information under the tested assumptions. It is not a measured radius ratio or a new eclipse-loss forecast. A full three-body fit with unequal radii and independent light-ratio or velocity information is needed. No new observations are used. Local fits, fixed limb darkening, approximate diagonal noise and a local track model limit the result. Code, source URLs and hashes, aggregate fits and numerical checks permit reproduction outside the signed package.

display.caption: Attained losses and geometry across eight fixed radius ratios in two QLP flux products. These are conditional local fits, not confidence curves.
